Of course, by rare I mean singular, as there's yet to be any actual game content featuring characters or world elements from Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 until now.

Announced in a Steam blog , Astral Ascent's Expedition 33: For Those Who Come After update is live now and free for all players, with the only requirement being completion of the main quest on base difficulty. Once you've got the update downloaded, you'll want to pop a seat at the new Campfire room, because you'll find some of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's best characters waiting there as special, themed summons.

Gustave is a support-type companion who heals you and gives you attack buffs, but he also has "a devastating" attack that charges up every time he's summoned. Maelle fights alongside you using a stance determined by your HP, shifting from attack to defense and unleashing a "powerful attack" that unlocks when she maintains the same stance for a while. Sciel is a card-based battler with mana regen, a basic strike attack, and a "powerful attack," each triggered under different conditions.

Meanwhile, Lune is an elemental spellcaster who syncs up with your own spell-using habits, and as is starting to become a pattern, she gets her own "powerful spell" when you summon her "enough times." Verso ranks up every time you hit an enemy and drops a rank with every hit you take, starting with an attack penalty and then building to a "massive attack bonus" as he ranks up. Finally, Monocco draws a random card from a set of five and unleashes a "powerful monster summon" based on the card he pulls.

Watch On There are also three new Expedition 33-themed rooms in Astral Ascent's crossover update: the aforementioned Campfire, the Lumière, where you square off with Petank and the Mimes with Lumière in the background, and the Gestral Village, where you face off against Golgra. Developer Hibernian Workshop says these rooms appear randomly before the final boss of each run, and you'll have the chance to pick between the Expedition 33-themed bosses or the usual Andromeda Bar, "but choose fast, it won't come back this run," warns the dev.

Getting to work with Sandfall Interactive on this crossover has been one of the best experiences we've had making Astral Ascent," the Astral Ascent team says in a statement. "Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is a game we fell in love with, like so many of you did, and this update is our way of paying tribute to it. Our biggest challenge was translating this world into our own pixel art, staying true to what makes these places feel alive while making them ours."

items.title: Xbox Game Pass is losing one of the best RPGs I've ever played, but you still have time to roll credits
items.summary: Don't skip playing one of the best games ever for free.
items.content:
You still have time to play one of the best RPGs ever for free on Xbox Game Pass.

One of the greatest RPGs of all time, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is leaving Xbox Game Pass very soon, but subscribers still have time to finish its story for free before it returns to its full RRP.

Released in April 2025, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 took the video game industry by storm, instantly becoming a leading Game of the Year contender. For the record, the Sandfall Interactive RPG pretty much made a clean sweep at some of the industry's most prestigious ceremonies, taking home a host of awards .

Without giving too much away, Clair Obscur has one of the most emotional stories in recent times. It’s set in a dark fantasy world inspired by Belle Époque France, where you follow Expedition 33 as they attempt to stop the mysterious Paintress, who kills people of a certain age.

Clair Obscur is leaving Xbox Game Pass on October 15, 2026. This should give you plenty of time to finish the story of this critically acclaimed RPG before it leaves the service and then you have to pay for it. In that respect, it also saves you $49.99/£44.99.

According to the aggregate website HowLongToBeat , if you focus purely on the story, it can be finished within 30 hours. If you want to do all the extras, you’d then be looking at 45 to 70 hours.

How many times have you looked at a game that’s free on Xbox Game Pass or PlayStation Plus and thought to yourself, “I’ve heard how great that game is; I’ll play that later”? But you never do, and when you do decide to play it, that game has left the service. You can’t let that happen with Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Don’t regret it.

In general, if you love the RPG genre, there’s every chance that you’ll fall in love with Clair Obscur. While it is a really unique game in its own right, its turn-based RPG combat does share some similarities with the likes of the Final Fantasy series, as well as Persona and Metaphor: ReFantazio .

That being said, since Clair Obscur launched last year, I’ve seen many gamers comment on social media and talk in videos about how this game is not only their first RPG, but specifically their first turn-based RPG, even for those who had no interest in the genre before. So, in other words, whether you’re an RPG fan or not, you need to give Clair Obscur a chance ASAP before it leaves Xbox Game Pass.

READ MORE: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 DLC dream teased, actor 'wants more'

On the aggregate website Metacritic , Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 scored 92 from critics and 9.4 from users. It more than earned its “Must-Play” accolade. On OpenCritic , it’s 98% recommended by critics and scored 100 from users, earning the “Mighty” accolade.

“There were moments I was brought to spilling a couple of tears, alongside some that had me laughing riotously. The battles, which can so often feel stagnant in a bustling genre, are refreshing, tactical, and delightful,” we said in our review, scoring it an “excellent” 8/10 .

“This is a wonderfully imaginative game, bursting with identity, and it has a lot to say about important topics. Yes, the path is a bit muddy and cumbersome, but the destination is worth it, and the journey is magical.”

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is available on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Comes To Astral Ascent In New Crossover Update
items.content:
We've been patiently hoping that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 would make its way to Switch 2 ever since it consumed our every waking hour last year. Sandfall is still yet to make that happen, but in the meantime, we have a crossover with the wonderful roguelike Astral Ascent , which we can play right now.

As revealed in today's Triple-i Initiative showcase, the sublime platforming roguelike has been treated to a bunch of crossover content from the land of Lumière. This includes three brand new bosses (Golgra, the Mime and Pétank), new rooms inspired by the game, and recruitable Expedition ally summons, each of which comes with its own special skills.

Truthfully, it looks wonderful. The crossover brings Expedition 33's world into Astral Ascent's glorious pixel art, and the trailer alone was enough to bring a tear to this writer's eye.

Here's the full rundown of everything included in the update, as detailed on the Astral Ascent Steam page:

Three Exclusive Bosses Golgra, the Mime, and Pétank have invaded the Prison, each with brand-new combat mechanics built just for this crossover. - Golgra - Calm at first, but her kicks and gestral allies get brutal once her second phase kicks in. - The Mime - Hammers, nails, walls take them both down together, or they'll revive each other. - Pétank - Runs, then rains projectiles, clones, and explosions on you.

Three New Rooms Straight from the world of Expedition 33 : Lumière , the Gestral Village , and the Campfire . One appears at random before the final boss each run: pick Expedition 33 content or the Andromeda Bar, but choose fast, it won't come back this run!

Around the Campfire Recruit a member of the Expedition as a special summon, each with their own unique mechanic: - Gustave - Heals, boosts your attack, strikes with you, and charges up a devastating finisher. - Maelle - Shifts stance with your HP; hold one long enough for a powerful payoff attack. - Sciel - Draws cards : Moon for mana, Sun for direct strikes, Twilight for a big hit. - Lune - Casts elemental spells matching your build, building to a powerful finisher. - Verso - Rank rises on hit, drops on damage taken, push it high for a massive attack bonus. - Monoco - Draws a random card, each triggering a different monster summon. You'll only get one Expedition ally per run, so take your pick, and don't forget to give Esquie a hug!

All of this is available for free to everyone who has beaten Astral Ascent on Destiny Level 0. What an excuse to dive back in, eh?

Original: Hibernian Workshop just announced a surprise update for Astral Ascent, which features a collaboration with Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. It can be downloaded for free on Nintendo Switch.

The main cast as well as iconic bosses like Mimes and Pétank are joining the platformer roguelite. The update features six new summons, three bosses, a couple of music tracks, and three different rooms.

Three Exclusive Bosses Golgra, the Mime, and Petank have made their way into the Prison. Each one comes with combat mechanics built specifically for this crossover, so expect to relearn your patterns.

– Golgra – She performs devastating kick attacks and small gestrals from the public jump in to join the fight. Everything is fine as long as she is calm but once she gets angry her second phase starts! – The Mime – They will be relentlessly attacking you with their hammers, nails, brick walls and more! You will have to defeat both of them almost simultaneously or they will revive!

– Pétank – Running away at first, Petank will then make projectiles rain on you, creating clones and big explosions!

Three New Rooms Step into three rooms pulled directly from the world of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33:

– Lumière – Fight Petank & The Mimes with Lumière in the background!

– The Gestral Village – Fight Golgra in her own village with Gestral cheering for the good fight to come!

– The Campfire – A restful and calm area for the Expedition 33 with their goal at the horizon: the Paintress & the monolith!

These rooms appear at random before the world-ending boss. Each run, one world is randomly chosen where you’ll be offered the choice between the Andromeda Bar and Expedition 33 content, choose wisely, because if you pass it up, it’s gone for the rest of your run!

Around the Campfire Pull up a seat. At the Campfire, you’ll be offered 3 of the Expedition’s members as a special summon giving you access to a unique mechanic!

Gustave: A versatile ally, Gustave heals you, boosts your attack and strikes alongside your basic attacks. Every time he is summoned, his arm charges up a little more until it’s ready to unleash a devastating blow.

Maelle: Maelle fights according to a stance system tied to your HP, shifting her focus between attack and defense. Hold the same stance long enough and she will unleash a powerful attack built around it.

Sciel: Sciel fights with a set of cards that trigger under different conditions: draw Moon to regenerate mana, Sun to have Sciel strike enemies directly or Twilight to unleash a powerful attack.

items.title: BF6 Reports for Duty on Xbox Game Pass While Clair Obscur Gets Gommaged in October
items.summary: Bluey’s Happy Snaps is also coming to Game Pass in October 2026 to put a smile on your face.
items.content:
Bluey’s Happy Snaps is also coming to Game Pass in October 2026 to put a smile on your face.

Microsoft Battlefield 6 is bringing giant battles and a whole lot of action to Xbox Game Pass on Oct. 13, which is good because a few days later, Microsoft is removing one of CNET’s best games of 2025 , Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Maybe Battlefield 6 and the other games coming to the service this month will be able to fill the Clair Obscur-sized hole in my heart.

Xbox Game Pass , a CNET Editors’ Choice award pick, offers a wide selection of games you can play on your Xbox Series X , Xbox Series S, Xbox One and PC or mobile device for as little as $10 a month . With a subscription to the higher-tiered Game Pass Ultimate ( $23 a month ), you can access hundreds of games, including new ones the day they’re released, each month.

Here are all the games Microsoft is adding to Xbox Game Pass in the first half of October 2026.

Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Oct. 13.

CNET’s David Lumb called this installment in the popular Battlefield series a “riveting shooter.” It’s full of huge multiplayer battles, close-quarters combat and loads of gunfights and explosions. While most people will gravitate towards multiplayer, there is a single-player campaign if you want a break from the online mayhem.

In this first-person soulslike game, you’re a soldier in Napoleon’s army who dies. No worries, because you’re back from the dead with a handful of supernatural abilities that you wield in your left hand, like in the almost 20-year-old game BioShock . You’ll use these skills to battle monsters and uncover a conspiracy that could threaten all of humanity.

Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Oct. 15.

Bluey’s Happy Snaps proves that not every game coming to Game Pass has to be full of action. You’ll unwind and explore Bluey’s world while taking photos in areas familiar to anyone who’s seen the popular children’s show – let’s be honest, this show’s also popular with adults. You can take photos on your own, or play with a partner, friend or your kid as you turn in-game moments into fun.

Those are a few of the games Microsoft is bringing to Game Pass in October. Here are the rest of the games you’ll see on the service soon.

Microsoft is also removing nine games from Xbox Game Pass on Oct. 15, including the award-winning Clair Obscur. So you only have a few days left to play through and explore these games before you have to buy them outright.

For more on Xbox, check out our Xbox Game Pass review , learn which Game Pass plan is right for you and discover what other games you can play on the service.

items.title: Say goodbye to the best RPG on Game Pass
items.summary: Sandfall Interactive's RPG broke records on Game Pass in 2025, but soon the RPG will be pulled forever from Microsoft's gaming subscription service
items.content:
Listen Thread 3 Add Us Link copied to clipboard By Patricia Hernandez Published Oct 7, 2026, 2:19 PM EDT Patricia is the former editor-in-chief of Kotaku , where she spent a decade writing and editing. Prior to that, she served as the Culture Editor at Polygon , and as a reporter at The Verge . Hernandez specializes in Pokémon TCG, Nintendo, and offbeat internet culture stories. News Sandfall Interactive's RPG broke records on Game Pass in 2025

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 3 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap It's a new month, which means that Game Pass's repertoire of games is due for a shake-up. The Xbox and PC gaming subscription service is getting a slew of notable new games, such as the roguelike platformer Neon Abyss 2 , Napoleonic soulslike Valor Mortis , and hit multiplayer shooter Battlefield 6 . More notable than the additions this October, however, may be the titles getting pulled from Microsoft's gaming membership.

Starting on Oct. 15 , Game Pass members will have to say goodbye to titles like A Plague Tale: Requiem, Donut County, and Pacific Drive. The most high-profile loss on the service is undoubtedly Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , the French role-playing game that swept Game of the Year awards in 2025 . For an RPG, Clair Obscur is on the more conservative side: How Long To Beat estimates an average playtime of just under 30 hours if you stick to the main story. The half the fun of any good RPG is the side quests — and depending on how many you take on, Expedition 33's play time can balloon up to 69 hours.

With its gripping story of a civilization on the verge of extinction and its flashy turn-based battles, Sandfall Interactive's debut game earned widespread critical acclaim last year. The game swept all the major video game awards in 2025, and it also broke a record for being th e most-played title on Game Pass that year .

If you haven't started it and have Game Pass, the clock is ticking. If you did start but put down the game at some point, there's slightly less pressure — but you still don't have long to reach the Paintress. If you have beaten Sandfall Interactive's beloved RPG, now might be a great time to check out the game's totally free DLC, Verso's Drafts . The expansion comes with a photo mode, fun new outfits, and some devilishly difficult encounters that must be parried. You could also try the game a second time around — knowing what happens actually intensifies the story .

And if, after all this time, you're still skeptical that Expedition 33 could really be as good as everyone says, you should read about how even high-profile haters changed their minds on it. If you already have Game Pass, though, you don't have to take my word for it!

items.title: Here are our Xbox Game Pass games for October 2026
items.summary: Battlefield 6 leads the charge into Xbox Game Pass this month, while GOTY-winner Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 finally waves goodbye.
items.content:
Image credit: EA News by Kaan Serin Contributor Published on Oct. 7, 2026, 4:55 p.m. 15 comments Follow Battlefield 6 Prioritise us on Google Microsoft has revealed the first batch of games coming to Xbox Game Pass this month, though subscribers only have a week left to try the award-winning Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 before it waves goodbye.

October's undisputed headliner is one of last year's hottest games, EA's Battlefield 6 . The large-scale shooter broke series records when it dropped, selling over 7m copies in three days and instantly topping Steam's best-seller charts . Post-launch updates and a surprisingly-involved Top Gun collab have kept the game chugging into this year too, despite layoffs at Battlefield Studios back in March.

The other highlights include seven all-new games launching into Game Pass straight away. Time-loop metroidvania Echo Weaver, road trip adventure game Forever Ago, co-op survive-em-up Deep Dish Dungeon, first-person soulslike Valor Mortis, cute photography romp Bluey's Happy Snaps, co-op roguelike Chained Beast, and city-builder (on the back of a space whale) Beyond These Stars slot into the service on the same day as their full launches.

But Game Pass giveth and Game Pass taketh away. This month's group of leavers include the widely-acclaimed and hugely-celebrated RPG, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, which debuted on Game Pass early last year. Some personal favorites, like Donut County and Pacific Drive , aren't sticking around either.

For more, check out our full guide to Xbox Game Pass and see every game in the service.

I have one eyebrow tentatively raised for Deep Dish Dungeon's moody, old-school world, if I can fend off the hordes in Gears of War: E-Day for long enough, that is - are you guys interested in any of the newcomers?

items.title: GTA 6 and San Andreas show how much game development has changed: In the '00s, Rockstar turned a Clair Obscur Expedition 33-sized budget into $600 million
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto's Hot Coffee controversy impacted its sales, too

Rivers carved canyons. And a whole bunch of other stuff happened between the release of GTA 5 and the impending launch of GTA 6 . In that time, developer Rockstar Games , in step with the broader games industry, ballooned in size and racked up expenses to match. But long before the days of production budgets estimated to be comfortably north of $1 billion, a new Grand Theft Auto could be built in a cave with a box of scraps – which is to say, developed in a few years by under 100 people on a reported budget of $10 million.

In the final run-up to GTA 6, a harrowing fact has struck the Grand Theft Auto community. Reshared online by veteran game developer Del Walker of Naughty Dog and Respawn fame, an archived news story from USA Today in 2006 notes that GTA: San Andreas had sold over 12 million copies roughly 16 months after its October 2004 launch. If you (somewhat generously) assume that all of those sales were made at the game's $50 base price, that comes to about $600 million.

This figure was widely reported in the storm of coverage orbiting San Andreas' famous "Hot Coffee" incident, appearing in other articles (like this one from NBC News ) that are still listed today.

Another figure helps put that gross revenue – which wouldn't translate directly to Rockstar or publisher Take-Two Interactive's share – into context. GTA: San Andreas was made on a reported budget of roughly $10 million, and we have two solid sources for that.

A December 21, 2004 article from The Wall Street Journal (paywalled) is cited by Wikipedia and references a $10 million budget for the game. Accounting for inflation, $10 million in 2004 is worth about $18 million in today's money.

Rockstar flashes its wallet, says GTA 6 doesn't compromise on detail or scale GTA 6 isn't too expensive for superfans, as 90% opt for the pricier $100 copy according to analysts Getting GTA Online players to move to GTA 6 is going to be "a mess" for Rockstar, Valve veteran says An issue of The Ottawa Citizen, an Ontario, Canada-based newspaper, was released on the same day and is also archived online (again, paywalled), with a relevant snippet pulled out and cited by the GTA Fandom wiki . It quotes then-Take-Two president Paul Eibeler, who left the publisher in 2007, as saying San Andreas was made with a budget of "less than $10 million."

It's fascinating to see this $10 million figure in conversation, because this cost threshold has recently been used as a soft reference point for what AA game development can look like – a mid-sized, responsibly budgeted and scoped game that punches above its weight, and a potential retreat for studios worn down by the boom-and-bust bets of today's AAA games.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Today, GTA represents the pinnacle of high-budget development, the kind of swing that only GTA can get away with, and the kind of game that only Rockstar can make at this scale and fidelity thanks to its pedigree, backing, and army of employees (and outsourced contributors). Oh, and GTA 6 costs $100 if you want everything in it – that'd be the Ultimate Edition – or $80 at base, which has become the new price ceiling for some AAA games.

As Walker puts it: "Finding out San Andreas cost like $10 mil to make, and made back $600 million without DLC, multiplayer or microtransactions, is like watching someone dunk barefoot." Meanwhile, the lion's share of GTA 5's ample profits were harvested through GTA Online monetization over several years. If anything, GTA 6 is first and foremost a platform for Rockstar's next big online component.

The most prominent touchstone here is probably Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a breakout turn-based RPG from Sandfall Interactive, a small French developer made up of mostly junior staff. Its budget was also under $10 million , just to put into perspective how much game development costs have exploded in 20 years.

items.title: Game Pass Is About To Lose Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 And Some Other Incredible Games
items.summary: The RPG sensation and more gems are leaving in October
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was one of 2025’s best games and one of the best third-party releases ever to join Game Pass day-and-date. Players have now had over a year to finish the turn-based RPG, but for any subscribers who haven’t yet taken the plunge, time is running out. The GOTY winner is leaving Game Pass on October 15.

That leaves you just under two weeks to go and complete the journey or start it from scratch. You can rush the main story to clear it in under 30 hours, but if you want to mine all of the expanded content, a completionist run will take you more than twice that. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the rare JRPG-inspired games that’s managed to break through in the modern era to a broader audience, in part thanks to its novel dodge and parry mechanics which inject some fresh energy into the usual turn-based grind. It’s also worth making it all the way through to hit the twist ending .

But Clair Obscur is also not the only great game leaving Game Pass this month . The full list includes:

Pacific Drive and A Plague Tale Requiem are both excellent, especially for the spooky month. The former is a sci-fi survival crafting game about navigating a zone full of strange anomalies with a haunted station wagon. The latter is about surviving a late medieval Europe infested with disease carrying rats. Donut County , on the other hand, is a light hearted puzzle game you can finish in just a few hours that is still one of my favorite indie games of all time.

items.title: Shuhei Yoshida told Expedition 33 studio to avoid terms like 'turn-based RPG' because it may cause people to "overlook" the game
items.summary: The perceived negative stigma around the term 'turn-based RPG' has led Shuhei Yoshida to advise Expedition 33 developers to avoid using it.
items.content:
Image credit: Sandfall / Eurogamer News by Sherif Saed Senior Contributor Published on Aug. 18, 2026, 8:29 a.m. 37 comments Follow Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Prioritise us on Google One of the reasons Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 stood out so much in early footage was how action-packed its combat looked, despite being a turn-based RPG. But while developer Sandfall Interactive has described the game as a turn-based RPG - and reinvigorated the genre, to some degree - not everyone was happy with that approach.

Veteran PlayStation executive Shuhei Yoshida revealed at the Busan Indie Connect Festival 2026 over the weekend that he warned Expedition 33 developers not to give the game that label (via Automaton ).

Yoshida was impressed by the game's combat, likening it to The Legend of Dragoon's, a game he was the producer of. However, his advice was for the team to pick a different term to describe the game, since he believed 'turn-based RPG' is an outdated term to some players, who could end up dismissing the game as a result.

"It's incredibly well-made, but it would be better not to call it a turn-based RPG. That alone might cause players to overlook it," Yoshida said, as reported by 4Gamer .

Yoshida, who worked as an advisor to publishers and developers around the time of his departure from PlayStation in 2025 , revealed the anecdote in a panel aimed at helping indie developers pick the right publisher for their games and making a convincing pitch. As part of his consulting work, he worked with Expedition 33 publisher Kepler Interactive, where he got to play a demo of the game two years before its launch.

According to the report, Kepler and Sandfall took his advice, using the more modern 'reactive turn-based battles' term to describe the game's combat instead. As anyone who played the game will attest, Expedition 33's brand of turn-based combat, which melds real-time mechanics like parrying and dodging with traditional turn orders, became one of the strongest and most-lauded aspects of the game .

Regardless of how much you think Yoshida's advice helped, the success of the game is hard to deny. Expedition 33 initially managed to sell a fitting 3.3 million copies in its first month , before bumping that to 5.5 million copies by October 2025.

It's also been one of the highest-rated games of 2025, winning multiple honours at The Game Awards that year, and ending up at number two on Eurogamer's list of the 50 best games of 2025 .

items.title: 'It's Incredibly Well-Made, But…' — Former PlayStation Boss Warned Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Devs It Would Be 'Overlooked' if They Called It a Turn-Based RPG
items.summary: Former PlayStation lead Shuhei Yoshida warned the developers behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 about calling it a "turn-based RPG" because "that alone might cause players to overlook it.
items.content:
Former PlayStation lead Shuhei Yoshida warned the developers behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 about calling it a "turn-based RPG" because "that alone might cause players to overlook it."

Yoshida, who served as PlayStation's head of indies and president of Sony Interactive Entertainment Worldwide Studios before stepping down in 2024, spoke about some key advice he gave the award-winning team during a recent lecture for indie game developers. Portions of that lecture were then reported by 4Gamer and subsequently translated by Automaton , including one piece of advice he gave to publisher Kepler Interactive while advising the team ahead of its April 2025 launch.

"It’s incredibly well-made, but it would be better not to call it a turn-based RPG," Yoshida warned the Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 devs. "That alone might cause players to overlook it."

But why? Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 went on to receive praise from fans and critics (including a 9/10 review from IGN), while ending its already explosive year with big wins across The Game Awards , BAFTA , DICE , and IGN award shows. Its positive reception was so intense that even the developers at Sandfall Interactive weren't prepared for its towering Metacritic score .

Yoshida acknowledged Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 as a quality release long before it reached the hands of the public. He was impressed early on, calling attention to its "combination of turn-based JRPG mechanics and real-time action inputs reminiscent of The Legend of Dragoon." The problem, however, was that, at the time, he was concerned its success could be affected by what he observed to be a tendency for turn-based JRPGs to be seen as outdated.

Game-award-winning formula or not, Yoshida feared Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 would be ignored by some gamers if they saw that "turn-based" label. As a result, Kepler got creative and instead started selling Sandfall's first game as an experience with "reactive turn-based battles" instead, and the rest is history.

The game, of course, went on to become a massive sales success despite its proximity to the launch of The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion . Yoshida said he's since noticed an uptick in reports from publishers receiving pitches for new turn-based RPGs.

While we wait to see what's next from Yoshida and Sandfall, you can see why the developers behind Final Fantasy Resonance think turn-based RPGs are making a huge comeback . You can also read the devs' conversation about canon endings and the writer who got their start at Sandfall .

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!
items.summary: Expeditioners! Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text! This brings the total number of supported langua
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: 1st Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: Expeditioners!! Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special
items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team

items.content:
Expeditioners!

Thank you for all of your reports - the details for the fixes in this patch are written out below:

Update On Sirene Crash

  • After a thorough internal investigation, the crash that occurred after defeating Sirene can no longer be reproduced on our end. If you keep getting this issue, we’d suggest updating your Windows to the latest version. If the issue persists, please submit a report and we’ll continue investigating.

    [/*]

Bug Fixes & Improvements

Photo Mode

  • Fixed facial hair of characters being blurred in the Photo Mode on the close distance if Shading was set to Epic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue in Photo mode that prevented the Inner Cone Angle and Outer Cone Angle options from affecting the shape of the preview light source.

    [/*]

  • Photo Mode's spotlight and point light display has been modified to improve their visibility

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where loading a save while picking up a journal could cause that journal to disappear permanently and become impossible to collect again.

    • Missing journals are now also restored retroactively when loading affected saves.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed a soft lock that could occur, during the Chromatic Glissando encounter in Sirene’s Dress level, when a dead expeditioner equipped with Shortcut and Second Chance pictos was swallowed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on Gestral Beach where using the Rematch option after losing the volleyball minigame could create a blocked save.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a visual issue where characters affected by Inverted would not have the correct colour effect applied to their eyes.

    [/*]

Environment

  • Fixed various environment issues (collisions, misplaced assets, missing or incorrect footsteps SFX) across Verso's Drafts, the World Map, and other levels.

    [/*]

  • Fixed various lighting issues on Steam Deck in Verso’s Drafts, Endless Tower and Stone Wave Cliffs levels.

    [/*]

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - We'll continue monitoring the reports coming in and working on future fixes!

~ The Expedition 33 Team
